texte.Un pays est signalé quand il réunit les: A country is flagged when it meets BOTH conditions: (#) its climate designed the cooling for a mild summer — Nordic or temperate class; (#) water is under strain there, either through the drought hazard at the chosen horizon (high or very high level), or through national water stress already classed as high. A southern country is never flagged: not because it is spared, but because its design point was set for heat. At the horizon shown,

texte.classes latitudinales — PUE par mode (da: latitudinal classes — PUE by mode (datacentres.py) — Nordic=#, temperate=#, southern=# — the class says how many hours a year the outside air stays below the direct free cooling threshold (~#-# °C, ADEME); beyond that, air conditioning takes over and, depending on the design, water with it. ⚠ THIS SCORE MEASURES AN OPPORTUNITY, NOT RESILIENCE: it says what is saved on ordinary days, never whether the installation holds on the hottest day. The failures observed occurred in a TEMPERATE climate — Rennes, Pantin, London — precisely where the sizing assumed mild summers. See “design point” and the heat × water conjunction
